title: Zero-Sum Thinking and the Roots of U.S. Political Differences
discussion_signal: The post relays the connection between zero-sum beliefs, policy preferences, and individual and ancestral experiences, presenting perceived group competition as a historically shaped political lens rather than a purely current partisan attitude.
linked_research_question: How do lived and inherited historical experiences shape whether people interpret social gains as positive-sum or as competition between groups?
limits: Post summarizes associations and does not establish a single causal pathway
The post's political interpretation may extend beyond the paper's estimates
